text:
pam: Quick sync note: proposing a fallback-graph instead of linear chains. Each node is a mitigation (cache, low-precision, rate-limit, rollback) and edges have conditions + priority. Want feedback.

raj: Graph lets us express parallel mitigations (apply cache + low-precision together). Good for nuanced degradation.

cory: How do we avoid combinatorial explosion? We should limit graph to shallow depth and require validated nodes.

pam: Agreed. Plan: max_width=3, max_depth=3, nodes must have validation_token. Also canonicalize node types to avoid duplicates.

raj: Decision logic? Walk graph from root; evaluate edges' predicates using EWMA-smoothed signals. Stop at first node whose predicates trip and apply.

cory: Add min_hold per node and global_concurrency_budget. Also a 'preferred mitigation set' for high-QPS routes that only allow nondestructive mitigations.

sre-bot: note created: INF-2077 fallback-graph-schema + simulation harness

pam: Telemetry: log node_id, edge_eval_scores, EWMA values, and dwell_remaining. UI should render small DAG and last transition.

raj: We must preserve A/B assignment integrity. Any node that changes assignment requires explicit flag and audit.

cory: Autoscaler interaction: if node reduces CPU, set scale_pause_on_recover to avoid flip-flop.

pam: Cool. I'll write the schema draft tonight with examples and a simple simulator to run replay traces. Thanks.
